summary.quality_check_rule: season left unobserved if the desert background is above -21.0 dB on every date or the threshold exceeds 6.0 dB

pumping_head.rule: head = static depth to water + drawdown + pivot pressure (pivots only)
pumping_head.detail: Pumping electricity per field = pumped water x rho g x head / pump wire-to-water efficiency (pump_wire_to_water_eff). Head = the static depth to water of the field's lift region (lift_m in data/national/official_2024.json; Riyadh fields south of 21.5 N use Wadi Dawasir, regions without a depth source the fallback) + drawdown_m + pivot_pressure_head_m on centre pivots that are not palm groves (model/params.json), all at the same level (low, central, high). Pivot-shaped palm groves get no pivot pressure: palm groves are not sprinkler pivots (the scenarios' pivot retrofit leaves them out too); on the radar + Sentinel-2 tier the tier's own class decides. Arabian Shield fields get water but no energy.
pumping_head.pivot_rule: centre pivot = circularity above 0.75 and at least 10 ha (the rule of scripts/region_pipeline.py and scripts/s2_fields.py); pivot pressure goes to centre pivots that are not palm groves, since palm groves are not sprinkler pivots

notes._shield: Arabian Shield regions (Makkah, Madinah, Asir, Jazan, Najran, Al-Baha): shallow alluvial or rainfed/spate systems; pumping energy is not estimated, so their zero energy is a lower bound. Lifted by the fallback head, the irrigated Shield fields (Jazan) would need about 0.13 TWh a year at central (0.06-0.25 TWh; see shield_no_energy)
notes._age: The depths were measured between 1979 and 2009 (Hail undated). Water levels have fallen since, by about 1-4 m a year where measured, so today's lifts are probably deeper. Static depth is about 87% of the pumping head used here, so adding the measured declines would raise pumping electricity by roughly 16-25%

palm_grove_pivots.rule: pivot-shaped palm groves (is_pivot, class palm_grove) get no pivot pressure; pressure_elec_kwh_not_charged is what the pivot pressure head would add on their water outside the Arabian Shield (in no total)

pumping_head.components_rule: the radar-only electricity split by head component (fields outside the Arabian Shield; the three add up to elec_kwh); pivot_fields, pivot_ha and pivot_share_of_pumped_water count the pivots that carry pivot pressure (pivot_rule: palm groves left out); mean_head_m and pivot_share_of_pumped_water are weighted by the water pumped outside the Shield

worldcover_filter.rule: fields whose ESA WorldCover v200 majority class (fields_labels.tif against worldcover.tif, 40 m) is mangrove (95), herbaceous wetland (90) or open water (80) are dropped; built-up (50) is kept

field_size.rule: Green patches (seasonal maximum NDVI above 0.40 in winter or summer, after a one-pixel opening) of at least 18 pixels (2.88 ha at 40 m) are kept, then a watershed cuts touching fields apart; the cut pieces can be smaller (the smallest field is 0.80 ha). Fields under 3 ha are kept: they are parts of real patches, so dropping them would remove farmed area.

shield_no_energy.note: Arabian Shield regions (Makkah, Madinah, Asir, Jazan, Najran, Al-Baha): shallow alluvial or rainfed/spate systems; pumping energy is not estimated, so their zero energy is a lower bound. Lifted by the fallback head, the irrigated Shield fields (Jazan) would need about 0.13 TWh a year at central (0.06-0.25 TWh; see shield_no_energy)
shield_no_energy.indicative_rule: not in any total: the same water pumped against the fallback head (head = static depth to water + drawdown + pivot pressure (pivots only)): fallback static depth 90/111/121 m (the Qassim range) + drawdown 4/10/20 m + pivot pressure 10.5/17.6/25.4 m on pivots that are not palm groves, to size what the electricity, CO2 and MW totals leave out

classification_range.rule: Every region's desert threshold shifted by -1 dB (looser: more fields active) and +1 dB (stricter: fewer) on the stored per-field HV above the desert median, in every season the quality check accepts; the same season, palm, class and accounting rules as the radar-only totals (including the pumping head: head = static depth to water + drawdown + pivot pressure (pivots only)), at the same low/central/high factors. Shifting by 0 dB reproduces the published flags.

zero_shift_check.why_not_100: thresholds and HV values are stored rounded to 0.01 dB

classification_range.corners_rule: low = minimum over {-1 dB, published, +1 dB} of the low-factor total; high = maximum of the high-factor total

s2_filled.rule: Radar + Sentinel-2 tier, published next to the radar-only totals and never replacing them; the area it adds is measured by Sentinel-2, not by the radar. Green = the field's median seasonal-maximum NDVI above 0.40 (s2_winter_active over 1 Nov-15 Mar, s2_summer_active over 10 Jun-31 Oct). (a) Winter fill: a field the radar calls not farmed in any season it observed (radar idle: winter observed and not active, summer not active or not observed) that Sentinel-2 sees green over 1 Nov-15 Mar and not green over 10 Jun-31 Oct counts as winter-farmed (audit nd-8). Fields the radar sees farmed in summer are not filled. (b) Outside the Arabian Shield, the season the radar did not observe on a partly-seen field takes the Sentinel-2 flag for that season. (c) Outside the Shield, fields with no usable radar season (radar not usable, or outside the swath) are classified from the two Sentinel-2 flags alone, a separate tier. Every mapped field is green in at least one window (the field mask is Sentinel-2 green), so (c) counts all of its fields as farmed: an upper bound for them. (d) A filled field farmed in both seasons gets the year-round (perennial) depth only if the spring check marks it perennial (not brown over 20 Apr-5 Jun) and Sentinel-2 sees it green in both windows; otherwise it is a rotation (winter plus summer depth). Palm groves among the filled fields: tree cover of 30% or more, farmed in every known season and not brown in spring; radar palm groves are never refilled. (e) Wheat straw on fields that are wheat-pattern only through Sentinel-2 is capped per administrative region at GASTAT 2024 wheat area minus the radar wheat already there: the cap goes first to (a)/(b) fields, then to (c) fields, pro rata by area. Water, energy and CO2 are not capped; energy uses the same pumping head as the radar-only totals, with pivot pressure decided by the tier's own class (none on its palm groves).

radar_plus_s2_seasons.scope: all 60,132 mapped fields: radar classes with fills (a) and (b); the 5,019 fields of fill (c) keep their radar class (no water)

s2_only_fields.scope: only the 5,019 fields of fill (c): no usable radar season, outside the Arabian Shield, classified from Sentinel-2 alone

combined.scope: all 60,132 mapped fields with fills (a), (b) and (c): water, energy, CO2, straw, fronds and farmed area = radar_plus_s2_seasons + s2_only_fields (fields, field area and class areas do not add up)

caps.rule: per administrative region: cap = max(0, GASTAT 2024 wheat area - radar wheat-pattern area (winter-only + rotation)); Sentinel-2-filled wheat-pattern area is credited with straw up to the cap, first fills (a)/(b), then Sentinel-2-only fields, pro rata by area; a straw factor is null where the region has no such area

winter_fill.rule: radar idle only: winter observed and not active, summer not active or not observed; Sentinel-2 green over 1 Nov-15 Mar and not over 10 Jun-31 Oct

palm_spring_check.rule: filled and Sentinel-2-only fields become palm groves only if not brown in spring; these fields met the other palm conditions but are brown in spring

filled_two_season.note: filled fields farmed in both seasons: year-round (perennial) depth where the spring check marks them perennial and Sentinel-2 sees them green in both windows, rotation depth otherwise; year_round_extra_water_m3_over_rotation is what the perennial depth adds over treating every one of them as a rotation

vs_official.rule: each administrative region's tier totals against GASTAT 2024 wheat and fodder (year-round fields) and MEWA 2024 agricultural groundwater; an overshoot is a tier total above the official whole-region figure although the boxes cover only part of each region's farmland. wheat_ha is the uncapped wheat pattern; *_wheat_credited_ha is the area credited with straw after the cap. Water: [low, central, high]

coverage.rule: share of ESA WorldCover 2021 cropland plus tree cover in all region boxes (clusters of at least 1,500 ha cut into boxes of at most 0.6 degrees); radar results = at least one season passes the quality check; rejected = processed but no season passes. fields: share of the mapped field area on which the radar classifies at least one season, and both seasons

reproducibility.rule: Fields mapped by two neighbouring region boxes (shared pixels at least half of the smaller field), each copy classified against its own box's desert background and threshold under the national rules (quality check, WorldCover filter); agreement and Cohen's kappa between the two boxes' radar flags, weighted by the shared area, over pairs where both boxes observed the season. Sentinel-2 flags of the same pairs are the control (winter: over the radar's own dates; summer: Jun-Oct).

Feeds: wheat straw and palm fronds from the radar-mapped fields of the 60 processed region boxes, and cattle, sheep and goat manure modelled for all of Saudi Arabia; poultry litter is not credited (its char's H/C_org is at or above 0.70 on the organic-carbon basis, rule 3.5.1).

siting_check.rule: each siting run must carry level and basis; its straw and fronds supply must equal the summary's total at its level for its residue tier (radar-only totals, or s2_filled.combined for residue_tier radar_s2), within max(1 t, 0.001%); and its persistence must match params.json; otherwise no siting is exported

params._note: Every value carries its source. 'derived' = unit conversion or arithmetic on the cited values. 'assumption' = modelling choice, shown as such in the app.

plant_sizes_t_dry.source: design choice: small distributed units (5, 10 kt dry/y) versus larger central plants (25, 50, 100 kt dry/y), tested as scenarios

min_load_fraction.source: assumption: a plant is placed only if it can be filled to 80% of capacity

wheat_grain_yield_t_ha.source: FAO via Our World in Data, Saudi wheat yield 2015-2024 (low 2019, central 2024, high 2022) https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/wheat-yields?country=~SAU

straw_t_dry_per_ha.source: derived. Low/central: effective baled straw-to-grain ratio 0.4/0.5 (Drever 2021, in Lefebvre et al. 2023, Biochar 5:65, p.14) x grain yield low/central. High: IPCC 2006 Vol.4 Ch.11 Table 11.2 above-ground residue 1.51 x grain DM (0.89) + 0.52 t/ha at 6.80 t/ha, x 0.70 sustainable removal (Lefebvre 2023 s2.2.1)

collectable_fraction.source: 1.0 because straw_t_dry_per_ha is already the collectable amount (baled ratio or IPCC x 0.70 removal)

straw_dry_matter.source: Haulage only (straw supply is already a dry mass). Low: 15% small-grain moisture (Lefebvre et al. 2023, Biochar 5:65, p.14); high: Sedmihradska 2020 Table 3 (8.4% water); central 0.88 assumed between them

alfalfa_collectable_residue_t_ha.source: IPCC 2006 Table 11.2 footnote k: alfalfa residue is harvest losses and litter only (0.29 x yield), left in field; treated as not collectable

irrigation_mm_winter_only.source: Lopez Valencia et al. 2020, HESS 24:5251, p.5266: seasonal fields Q1/mean/Q3, water reaching the ground (Al Jawf 2015, satellite-model fusion)

irrigation_mm_year_round.source: Lopez Valencia et al. 2020, HESS 24:5251, p.5266: perennial (alfalfa/grass) fields Q1/mean/Q3

irrigation_mm_summer_crop.source: derived: half the perennial depth (irrigation_mm_year_round), the share this model already gives June-September for year-round fields. A June-October crop grows at peak evaporative demand, so the winter (seasonal-field) depth would understate it

pivot_application_efficiency.source: Multsch et al. 2013, GMD 6:1043 p.1049 (sprinkler 70%); Lopez Valencia et al. 2020 p.5256 (losses 12-20%, study adopts 20%)

pumping_lift_m.source: Al-Salamah & Nassar 2009, J. Appl. Sci. 9(19):3555-3561, Table 1: depth to water in 17 municipal wells in central Buraidah, 2006, 90-121 m (mean 110.8). The paper's text also gives 90-138 (Methods) and 90-131 m (Results); the table is used. Static depth: drawdown and pivot pressure are added separately

pump_wire_to_water_eff.source: UGA Extension C965 Table 1: Nebraska performance standard 0.885 whp-h/kWh = 0.66 (derived). A well-run plant, so energy is a lower bound

grid_kgco2e_per_kwh.source: Ember via Our World in Data, Saudi Arabia carbon intensity of electricity, 2024 (691.95 g) and 2018 (702.88 g)

diesel_water_kwh_per_litre.source: UGA Extension C965 Table 1: Nebraska standard 12.5 whp-h/gal = 2.46 kWh of water work per litre (derived)

diesel_kgco2e_per_litre.source: DESNZ 2026 GHG conversion factors: diesel 2.66155 kg CO2e/L + well-to-tank 0.62409 (derived sum)

road_circuity.source: assumption: straight-line distance (lower bound); 1.4 is an unsourced sensitivity, flagged in the app

truck_kgco2e_per_tkm.source: DESNZ 2026 GHG conversion factors, freighting goods: articulated HGV >33 t 100% laden / average laden / all HGVs average laden

char_yield_dry.source: Sedmihradska et al. 2020, RAE 66(1), Tables 3-4: wheat and barley straw chars at 500-600 C, as received / feed dry matter: barley 600 C 28.2%, mean of four 30.7%, wheat 500 C 32.6% (derived)

char_c_org.source: Derived from Sedmihradska et al. 2020 Table 7 char carbon of four wheat/barley straw chars (64.7-67.2%; mean 66.1%) divided by an assumed total-to-organic carbon factor of 1.007 (lignocellulosic class, Enders et al. 2012 analogues): 0.643 / 0.656 / 0.667

cement_retention.source: Reported, not credited: in-service retention of char carbon in cementitious products, envelope 0.85-1.00 on 60-80 year horizons (Bartoli et al. 2020; Zou et al. 2025; Schmidt & Hagemann 2026, C-Sink Standard v3.3 s12.3). Credited removal uses the soil persistence model for cement too (Puro.earth 2025 v2 rule 6.2.4)

palms_per_ha.source: Low: Saudi 8-site average 100 trees/ha (AL-Omran & Eid 2019, Appl Water Sci, doi:10.1007/s13201-019-0936-6). Central: modern 9x9 m spacing 121/ha (FAO 2002, Date palm cultivation, Ch.VI). High: traditional ~6 m spacing 270/ha (FAO 2002 Table 40)

palm_residue_kg_dry_per_palm.source: Low: 15 kg/palm/yr (Al Yahya et al. 2021, Energies 14:6048, p.1; moisture basis not stated). Central: ~20 kg dry fronds/palm/yr (Chehma & Longo 2001, cited in Burezq & Davidson 2023, p.9). High: 28.3 kg oven-dry fronds/palm, derived from Nasser et al. 2016 (Energies 9:374) Table 1

palm_char_yield_dry.source: Usman et al. 2015 (J Anal Appl Pyrolysis, doi:10.1016/j.jaap.2015.08.016) Table 1: Saudi date palm waste biochar yield 32.4% at 500 C, 30.9% at 600 C

palm_char_c_org.source: Usman et al. 2015, JAAP, Table 1: Saudi date palm chars, organic carbon basis (total C 72.3-72.9% less inorganic C; Puro 2025 v2 rule 6.1.6), central 70.8%

layer_manure_kg_dry_per_hen.source: Layer manure, total solids per hen on hand per year: low USDA NRCS AWMFH (2008) Table 4-16(a) as transferred (4.37); central IPCC 2019 Table 10.13A Middle East high-productivity hens 5.21 kg VS / ASABE D384.2 VS:TS 0.735 = 7.09; high ASABE D384.2 as excreted (AWMFH Table 4-11(a)) 8.11

cattle_manure_kg_dry_per_head.source: Herd-average total solids per head-year on the GASTAT 2024 herd (516,323 head, 92% in barn-housed specialized projects; 11,674 L per milking cow; GASTAT Livestock Statistics 2024 Tables 1-4, 1-7, 4-1). Low ~1,640 = IPCC 2019 Tier 1 split: Middle East high-productivity dairy VS (Table 10.13A, 8.4 kg/t/d x 510 kg, Table 10A.5) on the 257,803 adult females and the other-cattle rate (9.3 kg/t/d x 362 kg) on the rest, / VS:TS 0.85 (USDA NRCS AWMFH Table 4-5 note 3) (derived). Central 2,050 = ASABE D384.2 total solids by animal class (AWMFH Tables 4-5a, 4-8a) at the GASTAT milk yield; high 2,350 = same at 125 lb milk/day (derived)

small_ruminant_manure_kg_dry_per_head.source: Total solids per head per year: IPCC 2019 Table 10.13A/10A.5 VS (sheep 93.9, goats 91.1 kg) / VS:TS (sheep 0.83, AWMFH Table 4-13; goats 0.822, Zhang et al. 2013 PLoS ONE 8:e66845); high uses VS 72% of TS (Hayat, Odeh & Elshurafa 2025, KAPSARC DP KS-2025-DP28, Table A6)

collectable_share_cattle.source: Low = IPCC 2019 Table 10A.6 Middle East (1 - pasture share). High = 0.919 x 1.0 + 0.081 x 0.54 = 0.96: GASTAT Livestock Statistics 2024 puts 474,410 of 516,323 cattle in barn-housed specialized projects (Tables 1-3, 1-4, 4-1), which also report organic-fertilizer production from manure (Table 1-8). Central 0.90 leaves room for flushed or liquid handling (assumption)

collectable_share_small_ruminants.source: 0.534 x c_holdings + 0.466 x c_landless, with 53.4% / 46.6% of sheep and goats on land holdings / landless desert and town-outskirt holdings (GASTAT Agricultural Census 2015, Tables 6-1, 6-2); c_holdings 0.6/0.8/1.0 and c_landless 0/0.15/0.3 are assumptions guided by the feeding and grazing shares in Aljumaah et al. 2014, giving 0.32/0.50/0.67 (rounded). The central equals the IPCC 2019 Table 10A.8 Middle East drylot share (50%). No study measures how much small-ruminant manure is collectable in Saudi Arabia

collectable_share_poultry.source: IPCC 2019 Table 10A.9: broilers 100% 'poultry manure with litter', layers 0% pasture

litter_char_yield_dry.source: Bedded broiler litter: the 600 C measurements are 37% (Tsai & Chang 2021 s2.1) and 45.7% of dry feed (Song & Guo 2012, JAAP 94:138, Table 2); central 42.6% is Das et al. 2008 at 500 C, quoted in Song & Guo 2012 p.141

litter_char_c_org.source: Organic carbon of broiler-litter chars: low Song & Guo 2012 Table 2 TOC at 600 C (32.5%); central 39.6% and high 47% are assumed class values for carbonate-corrected litter chars (not measurements)

manure_char_yield_dry.source: Low: Cantrell et al. 2012, Bioresour. Technol., Table 2, dairy manure char at 700 C (35.0%); high: dairy interpolated to 500 C (46.4%); central 42.2% is an assumed class value at 600 C (Cantrell dairy and feedlot interpolated to 600 C give 40.7% and 37.6%)

manure_char_c_org.source: Woolf et al. 2021, Environ. Sci. Technol., Table 2: manure char carbon fraction 0.39 in all temperature classes; bounds 0.33-0.45 from in-window analogues

gastat_2024_totals.source: GASTAT Livestock Statistics 2024: sheep 22,055,779; goats 7,339,749; cattle 516,323 (Tables 1-4/1-5 specialized 474,410 + 4-1 traditional 41,913); broiler barn capacity 274,069,031; layer capacity 55,101,080. Agricultural Statistics 2024: date palms 37,565,146. Livestock Statistics 2024 (Excel, published 20 Nov 2025) Tables 1-4, 2-1, 2-2, 3-1 to 3-3, 4-1: broilers produced 1,316,175,048 (2023: 1,165,355,341); broiler capacity 274,069,031 places is the most birds held on one day; eggs 8.42 bn table + 1.89 bn hatching; milking cows 232,950; camels 2,235,296

soil_temp_c.source: Annual mean soil temperature of the region of first use (Puro.earth 2025 v2 rule 6.2.4, also for char in cement): 30 C central, 25-33 C spanning Saudi regions (Lembrechts et al. 2022 soil bioclimatic dataset). Low estimate = hottest soil (least persistent)

puro_pf_table.source: Puro.earth Biochar Methodology 2025 v2, Table 6.1 p.101: persistence PF (%) = M - a x H/C_org over 200 years, M and a by soil temperature; a stream with H/C_org >= 0.70 is ineligible (rule 3.5.1)

h_c_org_straw.source: Sedmihradska et al. 2020 Table 7, four wheat/barley straw chars at 500-600 C: molar H/C on total carbon (Puro Eq. 6.5) = 0.391; x1.007 organic-carbon correction for grass chars (Enders et al. 2012) = 0.394; x1.015 if all Ca and K were carbonate = 0.397 (derived)

h_c_org_fronds.source: Derived from Usman et al. 2015 Table 1 (Saudi date palm chars): H 2.11% at 500 C (1.74% at 600 C) over an assumed organic carbon of 70.8% gives H/C_org 0.358 (0.295); persistence 0.712 / 0.722 / 0.743

h_c_org_litter.source: Organic-carbon basis, which Puro.earth 2025 v2 rule 6.1.6 requires (C_org = C_tot - C_inorg; the low-inorganic-carbon shortcut is for wood chars only). Tsai & Chang 2021, Agronomy 11:1692, Table 1: bedded broiler-litter chars have H/C 0.69 (600 C) and 0.71 (500 C) on TOTAL carbon. They are alkaline (pH 9.7-9.8) and rich in Ca and K, so part of their carbon is carbonate and H/C on organic carbon is higher: up to 0.726 (600 C) and 0.752 (500 C) if all Ca, K and Mg were carbonate, and about 0.80 with Tsai's 600 C hydrogen over this file's central litter-char organic C of 39.6% (derived; range 0.70-0.80). 0.73 / 0.72 / 0.71 are estimates in that range, so litter char fails rule 3.5.1 (H/C_org strictly below 0.70) and earns no credit at any level. Contaminants: Puro's Table 3.3 soil limits (WBC-Agro) apply only in the absence of Saudi biochar or soil-amendment rules (rule 3.6.9(b)); use in cement (Table 3.2, BE3) needs only a heavy-metal declaration (WBC-Material; its PAH, PCB and PCDD/F limits still apply). The contaminant evidence is mixed. US broiler-litter chars exceed WBC-Agro for arsenic (25.1 / 29.5 mg/kg DM against 20) and copper (213 / 310 against 200) (Cantrell et al. 2012, Bioresour. Technol. 107:419, Table 5, 350 / 700 C). Saudi broiler litter (Korish & Attia 2020, Animals 10:727, Table 3, Jeddah, dry basis: As 0.0005 mg/kg or less, Cu 23-29 mg/kg) implies a char that passes As and Cu, while Ni (23-54 mg/kg in the litter, about 54-127 mg/kg in char at this file's 42.6% yield with full retention, derived) may exceed the limit of 100. A measured Saudi char is needed. 'upside' 0.69 is the previous treatment (the total-carbon value, persistence 0.579 at 30 C): a hypothetical upper bound, never credited. Two modules read it: model/national_siting.py for its litter-upside runs (central_litter_upside_50kt, central_litter_upside_boxes_50kt) and model/national_scenarios.py in litter_upside() for its C3_E1 litter-upside scenarios

_soil_use.note: Soil-use status of each feed's char against Puro.earth 2025 v2 Table 3.3 (WBC-Agro limits, rules 3.6.9-3.6.11), for the page. Use in cement or concrete (Table 3.2, BE3) needs only a heavy-metal declaration (WBC-Material; its PAH, PCB and PCDD/F limits still apply), and char in cement is credited with the same soil model (rule 6.2.4). The siting applies no contaminant screen: it credits every feed that passes the H/C_org gate (rule 3.5.1), with the outlet chosen by haul. 'stream' is the siting stream the feed belongs to
_soil_use.regulation: No Saudi biochar regulation was found, so Puro's Table 3.3 applies (rule 3.6.9(b)). Registration with MEWA is still required: the GCC Law on Fertilizers and Agricultural Soil Conditioners (Royal Decree M/47 of 15/7/1427 H, Arts. 6-7), in force in Saudi Arabia, requires registration and a licence before a soil conditioner is produced or traded. If MEWA applied the GCC organic-fertilizer limits instead (implementing regulation of 2004: Cu 150, Zn 350, Ni 50, As 15 mg/kg, pH at most 7.5), cattle- and sheep-manure chars would fail on Zn or Ni, and chars made at 500-600 C (pH about 9.6-10.5) would fail on pH, so biochar would need its own registration route

straw.note: Measured: wheat- and barley-straw chars at 500-600 C have As, Cd, Cu, Pb and Zn below quantification, Cr 2, Ni 0.8-1.6 and Hg below 0.1 mg/kg, and PAH below 0.5 mg/kg (Sedmihradska et al. 2020 Table 7; Czech straw), far below WBC-Agro

fronds.note: No trace-metal totals for date-palm char were found (Usman et al. 2015 Table 1 reports only Ca, Mg, K and Na). A plant char is expected to pass, but a Saudi frond char needs a lab analysis against WBC-Agro

cattle_manure.note: Measured: dairy and feedlot-manure chars at 350-700 C (Cantrell et al. 2012 Table 5, US) and cattle-manure chars at 500 C (Cely et al. 2015 Table 4, Spain) are within WBC-Agro for every metal reported

sheep_goat_manure.note: A sheep-manure char has Ni 99-110 mg/kg at 500-650 C, at or above the WBC-Agro limit of 100 (Wang et al. 2019 Table 1; Hunan, China); its other metals pass, and As and Hg were not measured. No goat or Saudi data. Treat as cement-only until a Saudi char is measured for Ni, As and Cd. Plant outlets in the siting are chosen by haul, and soil-use status is not enforced, so the siting sends some sheep and goat char to soil. Enforcing cement-only would change removal by under 0.5% to first order (sites fixed) and by 0 to +2% with sites re-chosen (50 kt central re-runs on the earlier manure supply), a negligible effect on the headline, because char in cement earns the same credit (rule 6.2.4)

litter.note: Excluded by the H/C_org gate (rule 3.5.1; see h_c_org_litter), so not credited in soil or cement. Contaminant status uncertain: US broiler-litter chars exceed WBC-Agro for As and Cu (Cantrell et al. 2012 Table 5), but Saudi broiler litter (Korish & Attia 2020 Table 3) implies a char that passes As and Cu, with Ni of about 54-127 mg/kg (derived) that may exceed 100. Layer manure (nearly a third of the poultry stream) is merged into this stream; measured layer- and chicken-manure chars pass the gate and WBC-Agro (Wystalska et al. 2023; Lataf et al. 2022), but it is not split out here

h_c_org_manure.source: Organic-carbon basis assumed (Puro 2025 v2 rule 6.1.6). Measured manure chars at 550-600 C: 0.28-0.43 (Enders et al. 2012 SI Table S3), 0.41-0.42 (poultry manure: Lataf et al. 2022 Table 4; Wystalska et al. 2023 Table 4), 0.72 (cow manure at 550 C, Singh et al. 2012 via Woolf et al. 2021 SI). About two-thirds of the manure stream (64% at central, with the GASTAT-based cattle factors) is sheep and goat manure, whose char has not been measured, so cattle-manure chars stand in. Low = the highest value under the 0.70 gate; at 0.70 or above manure would earn nothing

palm_frond_dry_matter.source: Haulage only: Usman et al. 2015 Table 1, date palm feedstock moisture 7.6%

litter_dry_matter.source: Haulage only: USDA NRCS AWMFH (2008) Table 4-16(a), broiler litter as removed, 31% moisture / 70% solids; applied to the whole poultry stream, although layer manure (about a third of it) is wetter

manure_dry_matter.source: Haulage only: USDA NRCS AWMFH (2008) Table 4-16(a), dairy manure scraped from earthen lots, 54% moisture / 46% solids

broiler_litter_kg_dry_per_bird.source: Bedded broiler litter per bird produced (applied to GASTAT 2024 birds produced, 1,316,175,048): low Coufal et al. 2006, Poultry Sci. 85:398 (228 g dry litter per kg live weight per flock x 1.40 kg); central Berry 1997 via MSU Ext. P3601 Table 2 (0.311 kg DM per kg live weight x 1.40 kg); high all excreted solids, IPCC 2019 Table 10.13A Middle East broilers (0.52 kg VS over 42 d) / ASABE D384.2 VS:TS 0.75 + GASTAT 2024 wood shavings 0.05 kg. Market live weight 1.40 kg (USDA FAS GAIN 2006) | High corrected to 0.71 = 0.52/0.75 + 0.021 kg GASTAT 2024 wood shavings per bird (Table 2-3: 27,287 t / 1,316 M birds)

layers_on_hand.source: Laying hens on hand: central = GASTAT 2024 table eggs 8,420,841,886 / 286 per hen (USDA NASS Chickens and Eggs 2023) + hatching eggs 1,890,623,330 / 232 per breeder hen (Aviagen Ross 308 PS 2021: 178.5 hatching eggs over 40 weeks) = 37.6 M (derived); low = all eggs / 286 = 36.05 M; high = GASTAT layer capacity 55.10 M (includes parent and grandparent flocks)

pivot_pressure_head_m.source: Discharge head at a centre pivot, added to the lift for pivot fields: low 15 psi = 10.5 m, central 25 psi = 17.6 m (Amosson et al. 2011 Table 1, 15-25 psi; the same value as the retrofit scenario's baseline), high 30 psi + 4.3 m pivot height = 25.4 m (Amosson: some applicators need 20-30 psi; height from Al-Ghobari 2014 Table 1) (derived)

drawdown_m.source: Drawdown of the pumping level below the static water level, added to the lift: derived with the Cooper-Jacob equation from the aquifer parameters in ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.10 Table 2 (40 m is an outer bound)

official_sources.G24: GASTAT Agricultural Statistics 2024 (published 30 Nov 2025), https://www.stats.gov.sa/en/statistics-tabs?tab=436312&category=124583 ; tables 1-3 (wheat), 1-4 (fodder), 5-1 (date palms)
official_sources.M24: MEWA Statistical Book 2024 (Arabic, Dec 2025), https://www.mewa.gov.sa/ar/InformationCenter/Researchs/Reports/GeneralReports/TheStatisticalBook.pdf ; pp.62-63 agricultural groundwater use by region
official_sources.lift: Static depth to groundwater (no pumping levels published); see lift_m sources per region
official_sources.mwan_streams: Odeh & Muslemani 2025, KAPSARC Discussion Paper DP64 (Dec 2025), Fig. 1 and text p.11: the authors' 2030 estimates from MWAN 2023 data (CAGR 1.44%), back-cast here to 2024 at 1.44%/yr; wet or dry basis not stated

Al-Jouf.source: Low: MEWA monitoring wells 2-3 in the Wadi As-Sirhan depression, about 62-67 m below ground in May 2015 (Othman et al. 2018 Fig. 6). High: Tawil aquifer, maximum 250 m below ground (ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.17 p.429, after Abunayyan & BRGM 2008). Central = midpoint (derived; no typical level is published for the Busayta farms). The earlier 200 m was a 1979 level near the Iraqi border, in a different aquifer system

Tabuk.source: ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.10 pp.307-310: most levels 50-150 m bgl, around 200 m bgl

Hail.source: Kahal 2024, JKSUS doi:10.1016/j.jksus.2024.103384 s2.1: ~220 m around Hail city, 54 m toward the centre; central = midpoint (derived)

Qassim.source: Al-Salamah & Nassar 2009, J Appl Sci 9(19):3555-3561, Table 1: Saq aquifer in 17 municipal wells of central Buraidah, 2006, 90-121 m (mean 110.8). The text also gives 90-138 and 90-131 m; the table is used

Riyadh.source: No depth source found for the fields at 44.2-45.9 E; the Qassim 2006 range (Al-Salamah & Nassar 2009 Table 1) is used as the nearest analogue and flagged. Alharbi 2023 (JKSUS 102847, 92-130 m) applies to Wadi Sahba at 47-48 E

WadiDawasir.source: ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.11: 90-100 m below ground west of the wadi (p.326, 1980s sources) and about 150 m in the farming area (p.327, Bashour 2009), falling about 3 m/yr; high = 150 + 16 yr x 3 m/yr (derived)

_fallback.source: No current depth found for the Eastern Region or Northern Borders: the Qassim range is used and flagged. ESCWA-BGR 2013 Ch.15 pp.398-399 gives early-1980s levels only (under 25 m in the Dammam, 160 m in the Umm er Radhuma)

lift._shield: Arabian Shield regions (Makkah, Madinah, Asir, Jazan, Najran, Al-Baha): shallow alluvial or rainfed/spate systems; pumping energy is not estimated, so their zero energy is a lower bound. Lifted by the fallback head, the irrigated Shield fields (Jazan) would need about 0.13 TWh a year at central (0.06-0.25 TWh; see shield_no_energy)
lift._age: The depths were measured between 1979 and 2009 (Hail undated). Water levels have fallen since, by about 1-4 m a year where measured, so today's lifts are probably deeper. Static depth is about 87% of the pumping head used here, so adding the measured declines would raise pumping electricity by roughly 16-25%

lift_notes._shield: Arabian Shield regions (Makkah, Madinah, Asir, Jazan, Najran, Al-Baha): shallow alluvial or rainfed/spate systems; pumping energy is not estimated, so their zero energy is a lower bound. Lifted by the fallback head, the irrigated Shield fields (Jazan) would need about 0.13 TWh a year at central (0.06-0.25 TWh; see shield_no_energy)
lift_notes._age: The depths were measured between 1979 and 2009 (Hail undated). Water levels have fallen since, by about 1-4 m a year where measured, so today's lifts are probably deeper. Static depth is about 87% of the pumping head used here, so adding the measured declines would raise pumping electricity by roughly 16-25%

mwan.confidence_legend: estimation based on assumptions from international benchmarks
mwan.streams_basis: KAPSARC authors' 2030 estimates from MWAN data, back-cast to 2024 at 1.44%/yr; wet or dry not stated
mwan.source: MWAN (National Center for Waste Management), national waste inventory, National Waste Management Strategy (2023)
mwan.streams_source: Odeh & Muslemani 2025, KAPSARC Discussion Paper DP64 (Dec 2025), Fig. 1 and text p.11: the authors' 2030 estimates from MWAN 2023 data (CAGR 1.44%), back-cast here to 2024 at 1.44%/yr; wet or dry basis not stated

fodder_halt.source: MEWA news release, 7 Jumada I 1448 AH: halt of perennial fodder cultivation in the sedimentary-shelf regions from 16 November 2026; seasonal fodder allowed under licence (Council of Ministers Resolution No. 66, per Argaam, 26 Jan 2026)
